r0010: The European Court of Human Rights (Second Section), sitting as a Chamber composed of:
r0011:
Mr	C.L. Rozakis, President,
		G. Bonello,
	Mrs	V. Stráznická,
	Mr	P. Lorenzen,
		M. Fischbach,
	Mrs	M. Tsatsa-Nikolovska,
	Mr	E. Levits, judges,
and Mr E. Fribergh, Section Registrar,
r0012: Having deliberated in private on 14 December 2000,
r0013: Delivers the following judgment, which was adopted on that date:
r0015: 1.  The case originated in an application (no. 21463/92) against Italy lodged with the European Commission of Human Rights (“the Commission”) under former Article 25 of the Convention for the Protection of Human Rights and Fundamental Freedoms (“the Convention”) by an Italian national, Mr Fulvio Lunari (“the applicant”), on 10 February 1993.
r0016: 2.  The Italian Government (“the Government”) were represented initially by their Agent, Mr Luigi Ferrari Bravo, and subsequently by their Agent, Mr Umberto Leanza, and their co-Agent, Mr Vitaliano Esposito.
r0017: 3.  The applicant alleged, in particular, that his prolonged inability to enforce the order for possession against his tenant, owing to the failure to provide police assistance, constituted a violation of Article 1 of Protocol No. 1 and of Article 6 § 1 of the Convention.
r0018: 4.  On 5 April 1993 the Commission (First Chamber) decided to give notice of the application to the respondent Government and to invite them to submit their observations on its admissibility and merits. The Government submitted their observations on 29 June 1993. The applicant replied on 27 July and 9 November 1993 and on 17 February 1994.
r0019: 5.  Subsequently, the Commission decided to adjourn its examination of the application pending the Court’s rulings in the Scollo and Spadea and Scalabrino cases. Those judgments having been delivered on 28 September 1995, the parties were invited on 12 March 1996 to submit additional observations, which the Government did on 3 April 1996 and the applicant on 14 May 1996.
